- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior), true outcome often overshoots and then corrects — cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.2–0.6); add 2–4% bias upward for next 30d.
- If last 3–5 sentiment values are trending upward, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% per sentiment step.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely missing a “mean reversion” signal — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., alternating +0.8 and -0.2), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by 1–2% downward.
